rows.title: Mortgage delinquency rate up 31% in Q3, driven by Ontario and B.C.: Equifax report
rows.summary: Equifax Canada's third-quarter credit report found the share of mortgages 90 or more days behind on payments rose to 0.32%. That is up 31.1% from a year earlier and the highest level since Equifax began tracking in 2013, with Ontario and British Columbia driving most of the increase. The report comes after the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate to 2.5% last month, its first hike in more than three years, and markets now see about a 63% chance of another quarter-point increase at the December 9 decision. About 1.4 million of Canada's 9.1 million homeowners have variable-rate mortgages, and Equifax estimates each quarter-point hike adds roughly $860 million a year in interest on those loans. Total consumer debt reached $2.74 trillion (up 4.68%) and credit card balances hit $136.2 billion, so higher rates are increasingly squeezing household budgets.
rows.fact: The 90-plus-day mortgage delinquency rate hit 0.32% in Q3 2026, up 31.1% year over year and the highest since 2013. Overall mortgage delinquencies are still below 1%, but the Bank of Canada's October hike to 2.5% raises payments for about 1.4 million variable-rate borrowers. Canadians' total consumer debt rose 4.68% to $2.74 trillion.
rows.outlook: Equifax's Rebecca Oakes expects delinquencies to keep rising depending on what happens to rates, though they could ease by mid-2027 if rates stay flat; first-time and younger buyers are seen as most exposed.
rows.why: 중앙은행의 금리 인상이 변동금리 대출을 통해 실제 가계의 상환 부담과 연체로 어떻게 이어지는지 구체적인 숫자로 보여 주기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It uses concrete numbers to show how a central bank's rate hike reaches real households through variable-rate loans and turns into payment stress and missed payments.
rows.term_def: A home loan whose interest rate moves up or down with the bank's prime rate, which follows the central bank's policy rate. When the central bank raises rates, these borrowers' interest costs rise almost right away.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (industry report, not a government release; no usable Canadian government/BoC policy item in the last 24h, as Macklem's Nov. 24 speech had not yet been given). Figures cross-checked with the CP24 version of the CP story and Equifax's own GlobeNewswire release.

opinion.title: Canadian Consumers: Bending, Not Breaking
opinion.author: Maria Solovieva, CFA
opinion.summary: TD economist Maria Solovieva argues that Canadian consumers are under strain but not cracking: real spending grew at nearly a 3% pace in the first half of 2026, and national mortgage delinquencies remain near historical averages. The stress is concentrated in Ontario, where the mortgage arrears rate reached 0.34% in August, nearly triple its pre-pandemic norm and close to the 0.43% peak of the 2008 financial crisis. She links this to three straight months of job losses, Ontario unemployment of 7.3%, and a record share of variable-rate mortgages (35%) that pass Bank of Canada hikes directly to borrowers. Buyers who purchased near the 2021-22 price peak are most at risk because their home equity is thinnest. TD expects Ontario arrears to level off around mid-2027 and then fall if the job market recovers, and it names widespread job losses as the key risk.
opinion.why: 실업률과 금리, 부동산 가격이 함께 가계 부채 위험을 만드는 과정을 지역별 차이까지 설명해, 거시경제 지표들이 서로 어떻게 연결되는지 이해하게 해 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It explains how unemployment, interest rates and house prices combine to create household debt risk, including regional differences, which helps readers see how macroeconomic indicators connect.

rows.title: US blacklists Megaspeed, Alibaba's Singapore unit over links to Nvidia scandal
rows.summary: On Monday the US Commerce Department added Nvidia partner Megaspeed and Apex Enterprise Solutions, Alibaba's Singapore subsidiary, to its Entity List, a trade blacklist. It also added other Megaspeed-linked companies in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand. US authorities have investigated Megaspeed since 2024 over whether it diverted advanced AI chips to China. Listed firms now need Commerce approval to receive US exports, and that approval is likely to be denied. The move came after public pressure, including criticism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Nov. 13 and from senators of both parties; Commerce had not added any entity to the list since October 2025, and Alibaba says the Apex listing is a mistake it will fight in court.
rows.fact: Commerce blacklisted Megaspeed, Alibaba's Singapore unit Apex and other Megaspeed-linked firms in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, so exports to them now need a license that is likely to be denied. Apex had lent money to Megaspeed through its Malaysian unit Speedmatrix, which had assets of about 8.8 billion ringgit ($2.14 billion) at the end of 2024.
rows.outlook: The Justice and Commerce departments said they would pursue any criminal conduct, Singapore says it will keep investigating, and congressional scrutiny of Commerce's slow action is expected to continue.
rows.why: 수출 통제가 첨단 AI 반도체 같은 전략 물자의 국제 거래를 어떻게 막고, 무역 정책이 국가 안보와 기업 경쟁에 어떤 영향을 주는지 보여 주는 기사입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how export controls are used to restrict global trade in strategic goods like advanced AI chips, and how trade policy affects national security and corporate competition.
rows.term_def: Government rules that limit which products or technologies can be sold abroad. Companies on the US Entity List cannot buy US goods or technology unless the government grants a special license.
rows.note: 24h policy item: Commerce Department Entity List action announced Nov. 23 (US time), due in the Federal Register Nov. 25. Key facts cross-checked with a second independent report. Chosen over Fed remarks because Fed rate-hike talk was covered Nov. 19 and Nov. 22.

opinion.title: A Hollow Gesture: The U.S. Blacklists Alice Huang-Linked Megaspeed — But Skips a Key Rule That Theoretically Keeps NVIDIA Chips Flowing
opinion.author: Rohail Saleem
opinion.summary: The analysis argues that the Megaspeed blacklisting may have little practical effect, citing Chris McGuire of the Council on Foreign Relations. Commerce did not apply the Foreign-produced Direct Product Rule (FDPR), which extends US controls to foreign-made goods built with US technology. Because Nvidia's chips are made in Taiwan, the listing alone does not bar shipments to Megaspeed, while other Chinese firms listed over AI chip access did get the FDPR. As a counterpoint, a separate Bureau of Industry and Security rule requires licenses for advanced AI chips and servers sent to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, which should still sharply limit Megaspeed's access. The author concludes the designation is largely symbolic, and notes McGuire's view that country-wide license requirements work better than case-by-case listings.
opinion.why: 정책이 실제로 효과를 내려면 세부 규정 설계가 얼마나 중요한지, 그리고 제재의 허점이 어떻게 생기는지 생각해 보게 합니다.
opinion.why_en: It makes readers think about how much detailed rule design matters for a policy to actually work, and how loopholes in sanctions arise.

rows.title: Consumer sentiment hits 7-month low as stocks slide
rows.summary: The Bank of Korea's composite consumer sentiment index fell 2.3 points to 103.1 in November, the second monthly decline in a row and the lowest reading since April. All six components fell, as lower share prices and higher lending rates squeezed household finances, and travel and dining-out plans weakened the most. Expectations for home prices a year from now dropped 6 points to 118, and consumers' one-year inflation expectations eased to 2.6%, a nine-month low, which the BOK linked to cheaper oil and government price measures. The index is still above 100, so households remain somewhat more optimistic than the long-run average. But the trend shows a falling stock market and rising borrowing costs are starting to weigh on domestic demand.
rows.fact: The BOK's composite consumer sentiment index fell to 103.1 in November from 105.4, with the current economic conditions index down 4 points to 78 and the six-month outlook down 2 points to 86. The savings index fell 4 points to 89, its biggest drop since April 2020, which the BOK mainly blamed on falling share prices.
rows.outlook: A BOK official tied the gloomier assessments to rising lending rates, continued stock declines and uncertainty in the semiconductor industry.
rows.why: 주가 하락과 대출 금리 상승이 가계의 소비 심리를 어떻게 위축시키는지 보여 주어, 금융시장과 실물경제가 서로 연결되어 있다는 점을 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how falling stock prices and rising loan rates dampen household confidence, which helps students see how financial markets and the real economy are linked.
rows.term_def: A survey-based score of how households feel about the economy, their income and their spending. Above 100 means people are more optimistic than the long-term average, and below 100 means they are more pessimistic.
rows.note: 24h official data release (BOK consumer survey, Nov. 24 KST). Figures cross-checked with the Yonhap report carried by The Korea Times. Distinct from the archived Nov. 23 stabilization-fund story.

opinion.title: Stock swings add to 'double tightening' fears as BOK eyes another hike
opinion.author: Kim Won
opinion.summary: The analysis argues that Korean households face 'double tightening': falling stock prices shrink their wealth and spending, while higher interest rates raise their debt burdens. Citi estimates households lost about 563 trillion won in stock value in the second half of the year, which could cut consumer spending by about 8.4 trillion won and take 0.2 percentage points off GDP growth. Citi's chief economist Kim Jin-wook says these losses could act like a 0.50-0.75 point rate hike. The Bank of Korea is still expected to raise its policy rate from 3% to 3.25% on Thursday, even though the effects of the July and August hikes have not fully shown up yet. Analysts also warn that headline growth looks inflated because soaring chip prices have increased the weight of IT manufacturing in GDP, and that relying on that figure could lead to excessive tightening.
opinion.why: 주가 하락에 따른 '부의 효과'와 금리 인상이 동시에 소비를 짓누르는 '이중 긴축' 개념을 통해 중앙은행의 통화정책이 얼마나 어려운 선택인지 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: Through the idea of 'double tightening', where the stock-market wealth effect and rate hikes squeeze spending at the same time, students can see how hard a central bank's monetary policy choices are.

rows.title: German Ifo business sentiment rises in November
rows.summary: German business morale improved in November, as the Ifo institute's business climate index rose to 90.6 from a revised 90.1 in October, slightly above the 90.5 economists polled by Reuters had expected. Companies were happier with current business conditions and also raised their expectations for the months ahead. That matches the strong rise in the flash composite purchasing managers' index published a day earlier. The gains were not spread evenly: sentiment rose in services and trade but fell in manufacturing and construction. Ifo president Clemens Fuest said the recovery of Europe's largest economy is continuing but still 'lacks breadth'.
rows.fact: The Ifo business climate index rose to 90.6 in November from a revised 90.1 in October, just above the Reuters poll forecast of 90.5. Firms rated both current conditions and their outlook more highly, with gains in services and trade and declines in manufacturing and construction.
rows.outlook: Ifo's president said Germany's recovery is continuing but is not yet broad-based.
rows.why: 기업 심리를 보여 주는 지표가 어떻게 경기 회복을 미리 알려 주는지, 그리고 회복이 업종마다 고르지 않을 수 있다는 점을 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a survey of business confidence can signal an economic recovery ahead of official GDP data, and why a recovery can be uneven across industries.
rows.term_def: A number built from a large survey that asks companies how good business is now and how they expect it to be in the coming months. When it rises, firms feel more confident, and that often comes before more hiring, investment and growth.
rows.note: Released in the last 24h, but by a private institute (Ifo), not a government or central bank; no new uncovered European government/ECB policy announcement was found in the last 24h. Sub-index figures cross-checked with a second report.

opinion.title: Unbreakable, German business confidence continues to improve
opinion.author: Carsten Brzeski (Global Head of Macro, ING)
opinion.summary: Brzeski notes that the Ifo index has now risen for seven months in a row to its highest level in more than three years, with both current conditions and expectations improving. He credits lower energy prices and interest rates, large fiscal stimulus, and the fact that the Strait of Hormuz closure hit other regions harder than Germany, putting the economy on track for its best growth year since 2022. He also points out that only about half of the planned infrastructure investment from the special fund was spent in the first nine months of the year, which could reflect bureaucracy, creative accounting or simply a lag. ING expects GDP growth of about 1.3% in 2026 and 1-1.5% in 2027, but Brzeski warns that a cyclical rebound is not the same as a lasting recovery. He argues Germany needs bolder reforms such as less red tape and lower taxes, plus a long-term strategy on affordable energy, education and innovation.
opinion.why: 정부 지출로 인한 일시적인 경기 반등과, 구조 개혁을 통한 지속 가능한 성장이 어떻게 다른지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
opinion.why_en: It helps students tell the difference between a temporary rebound driven by government spending and lasting growth that depends on structural reform.

rows.title: Singapore raises 2026 growth forecast after 6.1% Q3 expansion
rows.original_source: Reuters (Xinghui Kok and Jun Yuan Yong)
rows.summary: Singapore's Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to around 6.0% from 4.5%-5.5%, after third-quarter growth came in at 6.1% year on year. That beat the official advance estimate of 5.4% and a Reuters poll forecast of 5.6%. Growth was led by AI-related production and exports, especially in wholesale trade and manufacturing, as data centre build-outs proved stronger than expected. For 2027 the ministry expects growth to slow to 2.5%-4.5%, partly because key partners such as the US and China are expected to grow more slowly. Economists warned that the boom is uneven: retail and food and beverage remain subdued, job growth in modern services is weak, and new US rules restrict advanced chip shipments to the region.
rows.fact: Singapore's Q3 2026 GDP grew 6.1% year on year and 1.5% quarter on quarter (seasonally adjusted). The government lifted its 2026 forecast to about 6.0% and set 2027 at 2.5%-4.5%, while Enterprise Singapore raised its 2026 non-oil domestic export growth forecast to 30%-32% from 14%-16%.
rows.outlook: Maybank's Chua Hak Bin called the upgrade largely technical and warned of a K-shaped recovery, while OCBC's Selena Ling expects the central bank to hold policy steady at its January review.
rows.why: AI 반도체·데이터센터 수요가 작은 무역 국가의 성장률을 얼마나 끌어올릴 수 있는지, 그리고 그 성장이 일부 산업에만 쏠리는 'K자형' 경제의 위험을 함께 보여 주기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how AI chip and data-centre demand can lift a small trading economy's growth, and the risk of a 'K-shaped' economy where gains reach only some industries.
rows.term_def: A recovery where some parts of the economy, like AI-related manufacturing, grow fast while others, like retail and restaurants, stay weak. On a chart the two paths split apart like the arms of the letter K.
rows.note: 24h policy item: official Q3 GDP release and forecast upgrade by Singapore's trade ministry on Nov. 24. Figures checked against the ministry's own release.

opinion.title: Singapore Q3 GDP jumps 6.1%, growth forecast lifted to around 6% as exports boom
opinion.author: Eamonn Sheridan
opinion.summary: Sheridan reviews the upside surprise in Singapore's final Q3 GDP and the upgrade of the 2026 forecast to about 6%, noting that Enterprise Singapore expects non-oil domestic exports to grow 30%-32% in 2026 and 5%-7% in 2027. He notes that manufacturing, especially electronics, drove growth while chemicals and biomedical output fell. He argues that stronger growth supports the Singapore dollar and lowers pressure on the Monetary Authority of Singapore to ease at its January review, since MAS runs policy through the exchange rate. He adds that the export outlook points to continued AI electronics demand that benefits supply chains in Taiwan, Korea and Malaysia. He flags risks from the expected 2027 slowdown, heavy reliance on AI electronics if tech spending cools, and new US licensing rules on advanced chip shipments.
opinion.why: 환율을 통해 통화정책을 운용하는 싱가포르의 독특한 방식과, AI 수출 호황이 한국·대만 등 아시아 공급망에 어떻게 연결되는지 이해할 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It explains Singapore's unusual exchange-rate-based monetary policy and how its AI export boom connects to Asian supply chains, including Korea and Taiwan.
